e.etymology: From Hebrew, usually read as venom of God. In Talmudic and later Jewish lore Samael is the accuser and angel of death, often identified with Satan.

assoc.t: Lucifer's angelic name in the TV series Lucifer

e.note: In Jewish tradition Samael is the angel of death and a name for Satan; some people will hear it as a devil's name.

e.etymology: A modern American blend of the My- of Myla with Lani, the Hawaiian word for sky or heaven heard in Leilani and Kailani. It also works as a respelling of Milani.
In Arabic Yaman comes from the root y-m-n, which gives the words for the right hand, good fortune and Yemen. In Turkish the same spelling is a word for fierce or formidable.

A variant of Chastity, the virtue word from Latin castitas, purity, with one t dropped; some read it as Charity crossed with Chastity. It rose in the 1970s after Sonny and Cher named their child Chastity.
e.note: Often taken for a misspelling of Chastity.

e.meaning: pure, the traditional reading of Catherine
e.etymology: A spelling of Caitlin with the -lynn ending. Caitlin is the Irish form of Catherine, long linked to Greek katharos, 'pure'; Americans began saying it KAYT-lin in the 1970s, which produced dozens of spellings.
The Spanish word for crystal, used as a given name alongside English Crystal. Both come through Latin from Greek krystallos, 'ice, rock crystal'.

assoc.t: Louis Roederer's prestige champagne
1985 Venezuelan telenovela shown across Latin America

e.etymology: From Greek Theron, 'hunter', from thera, 'the hunt'. A ruler of Acragas in Sicily bore it in the 5th century BC, and Americans revived it in the 1800s. The surname of actress Charlize Theron is unrelated.

assoc.t: actress Charlize Theron (surname)

e.etymology: A 1990s American variant of Darian and Darien, names usually taken as offshoots of Darius, the Persian royal name.
A spelling of Emmett, an English surname from a medieval pet form of Emma. Emma comes from the Germanic element ermen, 'whole, universal'.

e.meaning: from Carlisle, the fort of Luguvalos
e.etymology: From the surname and the city of Carlisle in northern England. The place name joins Brythonic caer, 'fort', to the Roman-era name Luguvalium, from a Celtic personal name meaning strength of the god Lugus.

assoc.t: Carlisle Cullen, vampire doctor of the Twilight saga
city in Cumbria, England; also Carlisle, Pennsylvania
singer Belinda Carlisle of the Go-Go's (surname)

e.etymology: Isabella written with the Y of medieval Spanish Ysabel. Isabella is the Latinate form of Isabel, which arose in medieval Spain and southern France as a form of Elizabeth, Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
A respelling of Miley, the name made popular by singer Miley Cyrus, whose childhood nickname Smiley was shortened to Miley. Use peaked in 2008, during her Hannah Montana years.

assoc.t: sounds like Miley Cyrus, singer and Hannah Montana star

e.etymology: A Japanese girls' name most often written with the characters for 'small' and 'lily'; other spellings give other senses. American use peaked after the 2005 film Memoirs of a Geisha, whose heroine takes the name Sayuri.

assoc.t: geisha heroine of Memoirs of a Geisha
Hakutsuru Sayuri, a widely sold cloudy sake

e.etymology: From posy, an English word for a small bunch of flowers, itself a shortening of poesy. It joined the flower names of the 1800s and has also served as a pet form of Josephine; Posey is an English surname too.

assoc.t: posy, a small bunch of flowers, as in the nursery rhyme
baseball catcher Buster Posey (surname)
actress Parker Posey (surname)

e.meaning: avenger (Greek); also a form of Alastair
e.etymology: In Greek myth Alastor is a spirit of vengeance, and the word means avenger. The name is also recorded as a spelling of Alastair, the Scottish Gaelic form of Alexander, 'defender of men'.
namesakes: Alastor Moody (Mad-Eye Moody in Harry Potter)

assoc.t: the Radio Demon of the animated series Hazbin Hotel
avenging spirit of Greek mythology

e.note: Greek myth's Alastor is a vengeful spirit, and the best-known current bearer is a demon in the series Hazbin Hotel.

e.etymology: Pet form of Constance, from Latin constantia, 'steadfastness', and of other Con- names such as Concetta, Cornelia and Consuelo. Used on its own since the late 1800s, it peaked in the 1950s.
A 1990s American respelling of Sierra, the Spanish word for a mountain range, literally 'saw'. The C spelling borrows the look of Ciara, an Irish name meaning dark-haired.

assoc.t: sounds like Sierra: the mountains and the GMC pickup

e.note: In Spanish, cierra is an everyday verb form meaning 'closes'.

e.etymology: Variant of Marlene, a German blend of Maria and Magdalene made famous by Marlene Dietrich. In the US it is used mostly in Spanish-speaking families. A separate Soviet-era men's name Marlen joined Marx and Lenin.
From the Hebrew place name Beth-El, 'house of God', where Jacob dreams of a ladder to heaven in Genesis. English-speaking Protestants took it up as a given name, and it is a common name for churches.

assoc.t: very common church name; Bethel Music worship label
US town name; Bethel, New York hosted Woodstock in 1969

e.etymology: A modern American formation, most likely an elaboration of Jamie or a feminine counterpart to Jamal. The same spelling is an Arabic word for a university or assembly.
A compound of Ana, the Spanish form of Anna (Hebrew for 'grace'), and Lee, an English surname meaning meadow or clearing. Also spelled Annalee.
A modern American spelling in the Alicia and Alisha family, written to show a long 'lay' sound. Alicia is a Latinized form of Alice, from Germanic Adalheidis, 'noble kind'.

A phonetic American spelling of Gianni, the Italian short form of Giovanni (John), from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'. It appeared around 2012 with Jionni LaValle of the reality show Jersey Shore.
The name of the hero of the 2001 video game Final Fantasy X. It is said to be based on tiida, the Okinawan word for the sun.

assoc.t: hero of the video game Final Fantasy X

e.etymology: German and Jewish surname from Bauer, 'farmer, peasant'; an older sense of the word was neighbor or fellow dweller. As a first name it is an American fashion of the 2010s.

assoc.t: Bauer hockey skates and equipment
Eddie Bauer outdoor clothing (founder's surname)
Jack Bauer, agent hero of the TV series 24

e.meaning: armlet, an ornament for the upper arm
e.etymology: From Sanskrit angada, 'armlet'. Angada is a monkey prince in the Ramayana, and Guru Angad was the second Sikh Guru, renamed by Guru Nanak in the sense of 'part of my own body'.
A recent American coinage in the pattern of Jahmir and Nahmir, pairing the Rah- sound of Rahim or Rashad with the ending of Amir.
A modern American coinage that puts a Z on the pattern of Jaelyn and Kaelyn; Z names such as Zayden and Zaylee rose at the same time.
A recent American coinage in the family of Alayah, Malayah and Nalani, built on the fashionable -ayah ending.

A spelling of Waylon with the -lynn ending, which has made it more common for girls than boys. Waylon is a form of Wayland, the master smith of Germanic legend, spread by country singer Waylon Jennings.
A modern American coinage in the style of Jahmir and Amir. It spread after rapper YBN Nahmir broke out in 2017 with the song Rubbin Off the Paint.
A feminine-styled spelling of Murphy, the most common surname in Ireland, from Irish Ó Murchadha, 'descendant of Murchadh', a personal name meaning sea warrior.

assoc.t: Murphy's law: anything that can go wrong will
Murphy bed, a bed that folds up into the wall
